llm_reasoning.analyte_preparation_explanation: Vitamin C is treated as solid L-ascorbic acid with molecular weight 176.12 g/mol. It is dispensed as a separate analyte solid into the experiment vial containing the KCl electrolyte components, then dissolved during the required mixing step. No pre-prepared Vitamin C solution or pre-prepared electrolyte is assumed.
assumptions: Vitamin C refers to solid L-ascorbic acid, molecular weight 176.12 g/mol, loaded into a Quantos cartridge before execution.
Potassium chloride and L-ascorbic acid cartridges can be loaded into currently available Quantos positions 1 and 2.
Water is available as a pump-compatible liquid on syringe-pump channel 1.
Nitrogen is connected to the platform purge function and is available for the specified 300-second purge.
The stated final volume is the nominal prepared-solution volume based on 7.000 mL dispensed water after dissolution of the specified solids.
The electrochemical substation will execute its available pH measurement before and after the CV run and perform the specified working-electrode polishing operation.

concentration_calculations.calculation_explanation: For 0.100 M KCl in 7.000 mL: moles = 0.100 mol/L × 0.007000 L = 0.000700 mol. Mass = 0.000700 mol × 74.5513 g/mol = 0.05218591 g = 52.18591 mg. The planned 52.1859 mg Quantos dispense yields an actual nominal KCl concentration of 0.09999998 M, effectively 0.100 M.

For 1.00 mM Vitamin C in 7.000 mL: moles = 0.001000 mol/L × 0.007000 L = 0.000007000 mol. Mass = 0.000007000 mol × 176.12 g/mol = 0.00123284 g = 1.23284 mg. The planned 1.23284 mg Quantos dispense yields a nominal Vitamin C concentration of 0.001000 M.

llm_reasoning.constraint_validation_summary: This experiment uses two solid cartridges, below the maximum of eight, and one liquid-pump channel, below the maximum of four. Each solid mass is below the 200 mg Quantos cartridge limit: KCl is 52.1859 mg and Vitamin C is 1.23284 mg. Water volume is 7.000 mL, equivalent to 7000 uL and exactly divisible by the 7 uL pump increment. The 7.0 mL nominal final solution volume is below the 10 mL vial limit. One experiment vial and one electrochemical slot are used, below the maximum of three parallel electrochemical slots. Solid reagents are assigned only to Quantos cartridges, and water is assigned only to the liquid pump.
llm_reasoning.drying_explanation: Drying is not applicable because no analyte is deposited on the working electrode.
llm_reasoning.electrode_deposition_explanation: No electrode deposition is used because Vitamin C is measured as a dissolved analyte in the electrolyte. The gold working electrode is polished before the test, then immersed in the prepared homogeneous solution with the platinum counter electrode and Ag/AgCl reference electrode.
llm_reasoning.electrolyte_preparation_explanation: Load KCl into Quantos cartridge position 1 and dispense 52.1859 mg into one clean experiment vial. Load solid L-ascorbic acid into Quantos cartridge position 2 and dispense 1.23284 mg into the same vial. Dispense 7.000 mL of pump-compatible water from liquid channel 1. Add a stirrer bar and mix for 300 seconds using stirrer-bar mixing until all solids are dissolved and the solution is homogeneous. Purge the mixed electrolyte with nitrogen for 300 seconds, then measure and record pH before the CV measurement.
llm_reasoning.parameter_selection_logic: A 0.100 M KCl aqueous electrolyte provides ionic conductivity and chloride compatibility with the Ag/AgCl reference electrode while requiring only one supporting-electrolyte solid. Vitamin C is set to 1.00 mM, which is sufficient to produce a measurable oxidation response while limiting electrode fouling and minimizing the required solid mass. The -0.10 V to +0.65 V versus Ag/AgCl window targets the expected anodic oxidation of ascorbic acid on gold while avoiding unnecessarily positive potentials where extensive gold oxide formation can dominate. A 0.050 V/s scan rate, 0.002 V step size, and three cycles provide a well-resolved initial characterization and allow comparison of successive scans for adsorption or fouling effects. The gold working electrode is polished for three cycles before measurement. Nitrogen purging for 300 seconds reduces dissolved-oxygen background and limits oxidation of the Vitamin C solution before measurement. The platform should measure pH immediately before CV and after CV using its available pH-measurement capability; the expected initial pH is mildly acidic.
llm_reasoning.selected_mode_explanation: The requested configuration requires Vitamin C to remain dissolved in the electrolyte during cyclic voltammetry. Therefore, the analite_in_electrolite mode is selected. Both KCl supporting electrolyte and solid Vitamin C are dispensed directly into one experiment vial with Quantos, followed by water dispensing and mixing.

metadata.description: Characterization of dissolved Vitamin C (L-ascorbic acid) oxidation in a 0.100 M KCl aqueous supporting electrolyte using a gold working electrode, platinum counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode.
metadata.experiment_name: Cyclic Voltammetry of Vitamin C in 0.100 M KCl on Gold
metadata.user_prompt: Perform a cyclic voltammetry experiment to characterize Vitamin C as an analyte dissolved in the electrolyte. The Vitamin C should be prepared in the electrolyte and measured using the electrochemical substation. Use the available gold working electrode, platinum counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode. Select appropriate electrolyte composition, Vitamin C concentration, CV parameters, mixing/preparation steps, and safety precautions based on the capabilities and constraints provided in the system context. The resulting experiment must be directly executable by the CVLab platform.

cross_contamination_risks: Vitamin C oxidation products can contaminate the gold working electrode and alter subsequent voltammograms.
Chloride-containing electrolyte residue can affect later chloride-sensitive experiments.
Carryover is controlled by electrode polishing before this test and washing/drying after the test.
handling_precautions: Wear laboratory coat, safety glasses, and nitrile gloves while loading Quantos cartridges and handling solutions.
Avoid generating or inhaling KCl or Vitamin C dust during cartridge loading.
Keep the experiment vial capped or covered when not being actively accessed to minimize Vitamin C oxidation by air and light exposure.
Use the platform nitrogen-purge capability in a ventilated area and verify gas connections before starting.
Ensure electrodes are washed and dried between experiments to prevent carryover of Vitamin C or chloride-containing electrolyte.
hazards: Vitamin C (L-ascorbic acid) is a low-hazard organic acid but may cause mild eye, skin, or respiratory irritation as a dry powder.
Potassium chloride is low hazard but dust may cause mild irritation.
The prepared electrolyte is mildly acidic because dissolved ascorbic acid is acidic.
Electrochemical hardware presents pinch, electrical, and sharp-electrode hazards.
waste_disposal: Collect the post-CV aqueous KCl/Vitamin C solution in the designated nonhazardous aqueous electrochemical waste stream unless local site procedures require a different waste classification.
Do not return used electrolyte to reagent reservoirs or Quantos cartridges.
Rinse the gold working electrode, platinum counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode according to platform procedures after measurement.
